title: Ad people in the studio
summary: Ad executives gave vague directions to impress clients, so he winked at the players and they played the same thing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: So did you have occasion to be in the studio and the ad guy who thought he knew music was there and, “Okay John I want this to sound, you know, like the sun is coming up” and these vague descriptions and you’re trying to find music?

Yeah. I mean anyone who’s done jingles has had that experience. Because they are there to look good to the client. And so they’re trying to impress the client with their knowledge. Because they’re charging them all this money. And all the guys in New York knew this. So I would go in and listen to what they had to say, “Oh you want more blue or your want it subtle here” and all that. So I’d go out to the guys and I’d say, “Now listen guys, we have to make it a little more” and I would just look at them and wink. They’d know I was bullshitting. And they’d play the same exact thing and he would say, “Yeah, that’s it.” Or she would say, “Yeah that’s it.” And the other trick was when they didn’t like the mix, every engineer knows this trick, we give the producer a fader which did nothing. Now you say listen, I’ll be controlling the horns here, when that sound that you don’t, bring it down just a little bit.” And it gave them something to look to the client and say see I’m important. And it never failed. Anyone who’s done jingles could give you twenty stories like that.
